blocks.etymology: From dumb + ass. It is likely that ¹ass (= donkey), not ²ass (= buttocks), was the original sense within this compound noun (solid compound or open compound), but neither sense is precluded, and many people today may uncritically parse the term in the latter way, even if it is misapprehensive. Apparent analogy with forms such as hard-ass and big-ass would naturally lend support to the second parsing. A similar synergy can be seen in the fact that the terms buttload and assload originated as literally meaning a cartload and the load transportable by a single donkey (respectively), but probably most English speakers today would assume that their derivation involves the buttocks.

examples.vi: Bạn có muốn một tách trà nóng không?

examples.en: Would you please open the window for me?
examples.vi: Bạn có thể vui lòng mở cửa sổ giúp tôi được không?

senses.definition: Used to talk about an imagined situation or what someone wants to happen.

examples.en: If I had more time, I would travel around the world.
examples.vi: Nếu có nhiều thời gian hơn, tôi sẽ đi du lịch vòng quanh thế giới.

examples.en: I would love to meet your family one day.
examples.vi: Tôi rất muốn gặp gia đình bạn vào một ngày nào đó.

senses.definition: Used as the past form of will to refer to a future event from a past viewpoint.

examples.en: She promised she would call me as soon as she arrived.
examples.vi: Cô ấy hứa rằng cô ấy sẽ gọi cho tôi ngay khi đến nơi.

examples.en: We knew that the exam would be difficult.
examples.vi: Chúng tôi biết rằng kỳ thi đó sẽ rất khó khăn.

senses.definition: Used to describe actions that happened regularly in the past.

examples.en: When we were children, we would play outside until dark.
examples.vi: Khi còn nhỏ, chúng tôi thường chơi bên ngoài cho đến khi trời tối.

examples.en: My grandfather would always tell us stories before bedtime.
examples.vi: Ông tôi thường luôn kể chuyện cho chúng tôi nghe trước giờ đi ngủ.

senses.definition: Used to give advice by saying what you would do in another person's situation.

examples.en: I would not worry about that small mistake.
examples.vi: Tôi sẽ không lo lắng về lỗi nhỏ đó đâu.

examples.en: If I were you, I would take the job offer.
examples.vi: Nếu tôi là bạn, tôi sẽ nhận lời mời làm việc đó.

senses.definition: Used in negative sentences to show that someone refused to do something in the past.

examples.en: The car would not start this morning no matter what I tried.
examples.vi: Chiếc xe nhất định không chịu nổ máy sáng nay dù tôi đã thử mọi cách.

examples.en: I asked him repeatedly, but he would not listen.
examples.vi: Tôi đã hỏi anh ấy nhiều lần, nhưng anh ấy nhất quyết không nghe.

senses.definition: Used to express what you think is likely or typical of someone or something.

examples.en: You would expect the hotel rooms to be cleaner than this.
examples.vi: Người ta hẳn sẽ kỳ vọng phòng khách sạn sạch sẽ hơn thế này.

examples.en: That would be the postman at the front door.
examples.vi: Đó hẳn là người đưa thư ở cửa trước.

vi_block: Đã sẽ; trợ động từ will chia ở thời quá khứ.

examples: On my first day at University, I met the woman who would become my wife.
Hi! I thought I'd come over and introduce myself. My name’s Chema.
wiktionary.gloss: Used to form the "anterior future", or "future in the past", indicating a futurity relative to a past time.

examples: When we were younger, we would cycle out to the beach most summer Sundays.
wiktionary.gloss: Used to, did repeatedly, habitually; indicates an action that happened several times in the past (cannot describe continuous states, as in I used to live in London)

examples: I asked her to stay in with me, but she would go out.
wiktionary.gloss: Was or were determined to; indicating someone's insistence upon doing something.

examples: If I won the lottery, I would give half the money to charity.
I'd never do anything that went against my conscience.
wiktionary.gloss: Used as the auxiliary of the simple conditional modality, indicating a state or action that is conditional on another.

examples: I would love to come and visit.
Look at that yummy cake! I would eat that all up!
wiktionary.gloss: Without explicit condition, or with loose or vague implied condition, indicating a hypothetical or imagined state or action.

examples: I would ask you all to sit down.
I would imagine that they have already left.
wiktionary.gloss: Suggesting conditionality or potentiality in order to express a sense of politeness, tentativeness, indirectness, hesitancy, uncertainty, etc.

examples: It's disgraceful the way that they've treated you. I would write and complain.
wiktionary.gloss: Used to express what the speaker would do in another person's situation, as a means of giving a suggestion or recommendation.

examples: She looked as if she would be sick.
He's very security-conscious, so he would have remembered to lock the door.
wiktionary.gloss: Used to express the speaker's belief or assumption.

examples: Sorry, officer, I wouldn't know anything about the crime, since I was nowhere near the scene.
wiktionary.gloss: Could naturally be expected to (given the situation, the tendencies of someone's character etc.).

examples: Would you pass the salt, please?
Just reach me down that file, would you.
wiktionary.gloss: Used interrogatively to express a polite request; are (you) willing to …?

blocks.etymology: From Old English wolde, past tense of willan, predecessor of will. The loss of /l/ in this word is probably due to weak stress, as in should and could (though in the latter, the /l/ was due to the analogy of the former two).

wiktionary.gloss: Something that would happen, or would be the case, under different circumstances; a potentiality.

idioms.gloss: Used to ask the interlocutor what they would like to order, to buy or have a look at.
To want; to desire (used to form polite requests, suggestions, etc., followed by a noun [phrase] or infinitive)
A rhetorical question used to express incredulity: who would have guessed it?; who would have thought that would happen?
One should treat others as one would like others to treat oneself; an expression of the golden rule.
idioms.phrase: do unto others as you would have them do unto you

idioms.gloss: By good fortune; fortunately or luckily.
Politely asks someone in a vehicle to put on their seat belt.
idioms.phrase: would you mind putting on your seat belt

idioms.gloss: Used to suggest dating someone.
idioms.phrase: would you like to go out with me

idioms.gloss: An expression denoting surprise or lack of understanding due to reality being very different from what is the norm or expected.
In order to achieve something, it is inevitable and necessary that some sacrifices be made.
idioms.phrase: the cat would eat fish but would not wet her feet

idioms.gloss: Used to show that the speaker hates or strongly dreads the task in question.
Used to point out that the interlocutor is failing to do something relatively easy that they should be doing.
Said of challenging surfing conditions, often as an encouragement.
Expression intended to help a person facing a choice with moral, ethical or religious implications.
Said of a person who habitually mislays things.
idioms.phrase: would lose one's head if it wasn't attached

idioms.gloss: nearly; almost
Used to denote that the speaker finds another person sexually attractive.
A rhetorical question used to express incredulity or surprise: who would have guessed it?; who would have thought that would happen?
Indicates the speaker is annoyed that someone is not doing something they should do.
Used to express astonishment or incredulity.
Everybody would change their circumstances if it were possible.
idioms.phrase: claret would be port if it could

blocks.etymology: From writ (“written”) + small, by analogy with writ large.

wiktionary.gloss: Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see writ, small, smaller, smallest.
Miniaturized; on a small scale.
